question: What problem does the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow solve, and what does OpenID Connect add on top?
answer_hinglish:
OAuth 2.0 delegation ka protocol hai: user ek application (client) ko apne data tak limited access deta hai, bina apna password us app ko diye. Authorization Code flow mein user browser mein authorization server par login karta hai, server client ko ek short-lived code deta hai (browser redirect se), aur client woh code back channel par token endpoint se access token mein badalta hai. Isse token kabhi browser ke URL mein nahi aata.

OAuth sirf authorization hai -- 'yeh token is API ko call kar sakta hai'. Usme 'user kaun hai' ka standard jawab nahi hai. OpenID Connect (OIDC) yeh identity layer add karta hai: openid scope maango toh ek id_token milta hai (ek signed JWT jisme sub, iss, aud = client_id, nonce hota hai), saath mein discovery document, JWKS aur userinfo endpoint.

Is project mein dono hain: /authorize, /login, /token OAuth ka hissa hain; id_token, /.well-known/openid-configuration, /jwks aur /userinfo OIDC ka. Interview mein yeh line bolo: access token API ke liye hai, id_token client ke liye.
why_needed: Bina OAuth ke har third-party app ko user ka password dena padta, jo leak ho sakta hai aur revoke nahi hota. OIDC ke bina har provider apna alag 'who am I' API banata.
real_world_analogy: Hotel ka key card: reception (authorization server) aapki ID check karke ek card deta hai jo sirf aapke kamre aur gym ko kholta hai. Card mein aapka passport nahi hota. OIDC aisa hai jaise card ke saath ek signed slip bhi mile jisme likha ho 'yeh guest room 204 ka Alice hai'.
how_it_works: Client user ko /authorize par bhejta hai -> server login karwata hai -> redirect_uri par code aur state -> client /token par code + PKCE verifier bhejta hai -> access token (aur refresh token, id_token) milta hai -> client API (yahan /userinfo) ko Bearer token ke saath call karta hai.
in_this_project: src/server.ts mein route() saare endpoints map karta hai. handleAuthorize request validate karke login form dikhata hai, handleLogin code banata hai, handleToken (codeGrant) tokens deta hai, aur sendTokens openid scope hone par id_token bhi sign karta hai. Poora flow test/flow.test.ts ke pehle test mein chalta hai.

Token scoped aur short-lived hote hain
OIDC se login ka standard tarika milta hai
disadvantages: Protocol mein bahut saare edge cases hain jo galat implement karna aasaan hai
Redirects aur browser state se debugging mushkil hoti hai
common_mistakes: Access token ko identity proof maan lena (uske liye id_token hai)

question: What is PKCE, and why does this server require S256 and reject plain and missing PKCE?
answer_hinglish:
PKCE (RFC 7636) code ko us client instance se bandhta hai jisne flow shuru kiya. Client ek random code_verifier banata hai, uska SHA-256 (base64url) code_challenge /authorize par bhejta hai, aur baad mein /token par asli verifier bhejta hai. Server check karta hai ki s256(verifier) == stored challenge. Agar attacker ne redirect se code chura bhi liya, uske paas verifier nahi hai, toh code bekaar hai.

plain method mein challenge hi verifier hota hai. Agar authorization request leak ho (logs, history), toh challenge = verifier bhi leak. Isliye S256 hi lete hain. RFC 7636 kehta hai ki code_challenge_method na ho toh default plain hai -- isliye missing method bhi reject hota hai, warna plain chupke se aa jata.

Is server mein PKCE sabke liye zaroori hai, confidential clients ke liye bhi, jaise OAuth 2.1 aur Security BCP (RFC 9700) recommend karte hain. handleAuthorize mein challenge missing, method S256 nahi, ya challenge 43-char base64url nahi -- teeno par invalid_request redirect hota hai.
why_needed: Public clients (SPA, mobile app) ke paas secret nahi hota; bina PKCE ke chura hua code seedha tokens mein badal sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Dhobi ko kapde dete waqt aap token ka aadha hissa rakhte ho aur aadha dhobi ko dete ho. Kapde wapas tabhi milenge jab aapka aadha hissa match kare. plain matlab dono hisse ek jaise -- jo slip dekh le woh kapde le jaaye.
how_it_works: Authorize: challenge = base64url(sha256(verifier)) store hota hai login transaction aur phir code ke saath. Token: verifier ka syntax (43-128 unreserved chars) check, phir s256(verifier) ko challenge se safeEqual (constant-time) compare.
in_this_project: src/server.ts handleAuthorize: if (!challenge) -> invalid_request; if (method !== 'S256') -> invalid_request; CHALLENGE_RE check. codeGrant mein pkceMatches(verifier, c.codeChallenge). src/secrets.ts mein VERIFIER_RE, CHALLENGE_RE, s256, pkceMatches. Tests: authorize.test.ts ('code_challenge_method=plain', 'code_challenge without a method'), token.test.ts ('wrong code_verifier'), units.test.ts mein RFC 7636 appendix B ka test vector.
advantages: Chura hua code bina verifier ke bekaar
Public clients ko secret ki zaroorat nahi
Confidential clients ke liye bhi extra layer (code injection se bachav)
disadvantages: Client ko verifier session mein safely rakhna padta hai
Purane clients jo sirf plain jaante hain, kaam nahi karenge
common_mistakes: Missing code_challenge_method ko S256 maan lena (RFC ke hisaab se woh plain hai)
Verifier ka syntax check na karna
PKCE sirf public clients ke liye optional rakhna

question: Why must redirect_uri be matched exactly, and why does the server show an error page instead of redirecting when it does not match?
answer_hinglish:
redirect_uri woh address hai jahan authorization code bheja jata hai. Agar matching loose ho -- prefix, wildcard, ya normalisation -- toh attacker ek aisa URI bana sakta hai jo check pass kare lekin uske control mein ho, jaise https://app.example.test/callback/../evil ya ek open redirect wala path. Phir code seedha attacker ko milta hai. Isliye OAuth Security BCP exact string comparison bolta hai.

Doosra point: agar redirect_uri galat hai toh server ko us URI par error ke saath bhi redirect NAHI karna chahiye (RFC 6749 4.1.2.1). Warna server ek open redirector ban jata hai: attacker koi bhi URL dal ke hamare trusted domain se user ko phishing page par bhej sakta hai.

Is project mein redirectUriAllowed sirf client.redirect_uris.includes(redirectUri) karta hai. Unknown client ya galat redirect_uri par 400 HTML page aata hai, Location header nahi, cookie nahi. Baaki errors (jaise plain PKCE) tabhi redirect hote hain jab URI verify ho chuka ho. Tests mein 8 variants hain: missing, prefix, trailing slash, extra query, doosra port, case, doosra host, doosre client ka URI.
why_needed: Code ka destination hi galat ho toh PKCE ke alawa koi bachav nahi bachta; aur open redirect phishing ka seedha raasta hai.
real_world_analogy: Courier wala parcel sirf registered address par deta hai. Agar woh 'Gali 5 se shuru hone wala koi bhi ghar' maan le, toh Gali 5 ka koi bhi chor parcel le lega.
how_it_works: Config load hote waqt redirect_uris validate hote hain (absolute, no fragment, http sirf loopback). Request par string equality. Mismatch -> sendHtml 400. Match -> aage ke errors redirectWith se query mein error, error_description, state, iss.
in_this_project: src/server.ts redirectUriAllowed aur handleAuthorize ka pehla hissa; src/config.ts checkRedirectUri config time par. token.test.ts mein bhi check hai ki /token par bheja redirect_uri code wale se exact same ho ('redirect_uri different from the authorization request'). Mutation M1 (startsWith) ne 3 tests red kiye.
advantages: Simple aur predictable: koi parsing bug nahi
Open redirect ka risk nahi
disadvantages: Har environment ka URI register karna padta hai
Native apps ke loopback port badalne wale case (RFC 8252) abhi support nahi
common_mistakes: startsWith ya regex se match karna
Galat redirect_uri par bhi error redirect kar dena
URL ko normalise karke compare karna (encoding tricks)

question: Why are authorization codes single-use and short-lived, and why does a reused code revoke the tokens already issued from it?
answer_hinglish:
Code browser ke URL mein travel karta hai, toh woh history, logs, Referer ya kisi malicious extension mein leak ho sakta hai. Isliye use bahut chhota jeevan (yahan 60 second) aur ek hi use dete hain. Agar ek hi code do baar aaye, iska matlab hai do parties ke paas woh hai -- legit client aur shayad attacker. Server nahi jaan sakta ki kaun asli hai.

RFC 6749 4.1.2 aur Security BCP kehte hain ki reuse par request fail karo aur us code se jo tokens pehle issue hue the unhe bhi revoke karo (SHOULD). Kyunki agar attacker pehle redeem kar chuka hai, toh legit client ka second attempt hi signal hai, aur attacker ke tokens marne chahiye.

Is project mein code ka sirf SHA-256 hash store hota hai. codes.consume(hash) atomic check-and-set hai: pehli call ok, baad ki har call reused. Reused par code.familyId ki family revoke hoti hai: refresh token band, aur access token /userinfo par 401. Ek design choice aur: code pehli presentation par hi burn hota hai, chahe us request ka verifier galat ho.
why_needed: Leak hua code agar baar baar chal sake ya lamba chale, toh attack window badi ho jaati hai.
real_world_analogy: Movie ticket ka QR code: gate par ek baar scan hota hai. Agar wahi QR doosri baar scan ho, toh sirf doosra banda nahi rokte -- andar baithe pehle bande ko bhi check karte hain kyunki ticket copy hua hai.
how_it_works: Login par randomToken() code, sha256(code) store with expiresAt = now + 60 s. Token par consume -> missing/reused/ok. ok ke baad expiry, client, redirect_uri, PKCE check. Tokens ek nayi family mein bante hain aur setFamily(codeHash, familyId) se code se link hote hain.
in_this_project: src/store.ts MemoryCodeStore.consume aur setFamily; src/server.ts codeGrant ka reused branch revokeFamily karta hai. Tests: token.test.ts 'a reused code fails AND revokes the tokens issued from it', 'the code is burned by its first presentation, even a failed one', 'an expired code (older than 60 s)'. Mutations M4, M5, M6 sab pakde gaye.
advantages: Leak hue code ki window bahut chhoti
Reuse ek detectable signal ban jata hai
Hash storage: database leak se codes nahi milte
disadvantages: Legit client ka network retry bhi reuse lagega aur tokens revoke honge
Store ko reused codes yaad rakhne padte hain (yahan expiry sweep nahi hai)
common_mistakes: Used code ko delete kar dena -- phir reuse aur 'unknown' mein fark nahi pata
Check aur mark used ko do alag non-atomic steps mein karna
Reuse par sirf error dena, tokens revoke na karna

question: Explain refresh token rotation with reuse detection. What is a token family and what happens when an old refresh token is presented?
answer_hinglish:
Refresh token lamba chalta hai (yahan 14 din), isliye uski chori sabse mehngi padti hai. Rotation ka matlab: har refresh par client ko NAYA refresh token milta hai aur purana use ho chuka mark hota hai. Agar ek purana (already used) token wapas aaye, toh do mein se ek ne chori ki hai -- ya toh attacker ne purana token use kiya, ya attacker ne pehle use kiya aur ab legit client purana bhej raha hai. Server nahi bata sakta kaun, isliye poori family revoke karta hai (RFC 9700 4.14.2).

Token family = ek authorization code se nikli saari cheezein: uske access tokens aur rotate hote refresh tokens ki chain. Is project mein TokenFamily record hota hai {id, clientId, sub, scope, revoked}. Har refresh token familyId rakhta hai, aur har access token ka jti family se map hota hai.

refreshGrant mein order: lookup by hash, client match, family revoked nahi, expiry, rt.used fast path, scope narrowing check, phir atomic markUsed. markUsed false de toh reuseDetected() family revoke karta hai. Test 'reusing an old refresh token revokes the WHOLE family' dikhata hai ki newest token aur dono access tokens bhi mar gaye.
why_needed: Bina rotation ke chura hua refresh token 14 din tak chupchap naye access tokens banata rahega aur kisi ko pata nahi chalega.
real_world_analogy: Bank ka OTP chain: har login par naya OTP, purana bekaar. Agar koi purana OTP try kare, bank poora account freeze kar deta hai kyunki kisi ke paas copy hai.
how_it_works: Refresh: getRefresh(sha256(token)) -> checks -> markUsed(hash) atomic -> naya refresh token same familyId ke saath saveRefresh, naya access token recordAccessToken(jti, familyId). Reuse: revokeFamily(id) -> family.revoked = true; refreshGrant aur handleUserinfo dono family.revoked check karte hain.
in_this_project: src/server.ts refreshGrant, reuseDetected, sendTokens; src/store.ts TokenStore.markUsed, revokeFamily, recordAccessToken. Tests: test/refresh.test.ts. Mutation M7 (revoke hata diya) aur M8 (markUsed ne mark karna band kiya) dono pakde gaye; M8 par pehle sirf reuse test red hua tha, rotation test ab purana token dobara try karta hai.
advantages: Chori detectable ho jaati hai
Attacker aur victim dono ke tokens ek saath band, nuksan limited
Stored sirf hash, DB leak se tokens nahi milte
disadvantages: Legit client ka retry (response kho gaya) bhi reuse lagta hai aur user logout ho jata hai
Har refresh par write: storage load badhta hai
common_mistakes: Rotation karna lekin reuse par sirf us token ko reject karna, family ko nahi
Naya token issue karne ke baad purana mark karna (race window)
Rejected scope request mein token burn kar dena
follow_up_questions: Network retry wale false positive ko kaise handle karoge (grace period)?
Family ki absolute lifetime kyun chahiye?
DPoP refresh token chori ka kya karta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Rotation security deta hai par har refresh ek write ban jata hai aur client ko naya token atomically save karna padta hai. Family revoke harsh hai: ek galti se user ka poora session jata hai, lekin yeh fail-safe direction hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Client ko naya refresh token wala response network mein kho jaye -> client purana bhejta hai -> reuse -> family revoke -> user ko dobara login. Do tabs ek saath refresh karein -> ek jeetega, doosra reuse trigger karega. Yeh dono is project mein aise hi behave karenge; koi grace period nahi hai.
advanced.alternatives: Sender-constrained refresh tokens (DPoP, mTLS) jahan chori hua token bina key ke bekaar hai; ya rotation ke saath chhota grace window (kuch second) jisme previous token ek baar aur chale.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Har refresh ek atomic UPDATE hai; 100x par refresh_tokens table hot ho jaati hai, index on token_hash aur family_id chahiye, aur purane used rows ki cleanup job. Family revoke ek row update hai, toh sasta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Persistent store with UPDATE ... WHERE used = false, family absolute lifetime, reuse events ka audit log aur alert, client ke liye clear error taaki woh user ko login par bheje.

question: How does this server sign an ES256 JWT using only node:crypto, and what is the ieee-p1363 detail?
answer_hinglish:
JWT (JWS compact form) teen base64url parts hai: header.payload.signature. Signing input = base64url(header) + '.' + base64url(payload). ES256 matlab ECDSA on P-256 curve with SHA-256.

Node ka crypto.sign('sha256', data, key) default mein signature DER encoding mein deta hai (ASN.1 SEQUENCE of r aur s, length 70-72 bytes ke aas paas). Lekin JWS spec (RFC 7518 3.4) kehta hai ki ES256 signature raw r || s hona chahiye, exactly 64 bytes. Isliye signJwt mein dsaEncoding: 'ieee-p1363' pass karte hain. Agar yeh bhool gaye toh hamara khud ka verify chal jayega, lekin jose ya koi bhi standard library signature reject kar degi -- isiliye interop test zaroori hai.

Header mein alg ES256, typ (access token ke liye at+jwt, id_token ke liye JWT) aur kid hota hai. kid public key ka RFC 7638 thumbprint hai, toh woh key se deterministic nikalta hai. Key generateKeyPairSync('ec', {namedCurve: 'P-256'}) se banti hai ya SIGNING_KEY_FILE PEM se load hoti hai.
why_needed: Bina library ke JWT likhna tabhi safe hai jab encoding details bilkul spec ke hisaab se hon; ek byte format galat aur interop toot jaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Cheque par signature: bank sirf ek tay format maanta hai. Aap apne ghar ke register mein kisi bhi style mein sign karo, bank (doosri library) wahi accept karega jo standard format mein ho.
how_it_works: signJwt: header JSON -> base64url, payload JSON -> base64url, sign(sha256, input, {key, dsaEncoding: ieee-p1363}) -> base64url. verifyJwt: same encoding ke saath crypto.verify, signature length exactly 64 check.
in_this_project: src/jwt.ts signJwt, verifyJwt, signingKeyFromPrivate (P-256 check, JWK export, kid), jwkThumbprint. units.test.ts 'sign + verify round trip, 64-byte raw ECDSA signature'; interop.test.ts mein jose jwtVerify hamare /jwks se key leke access token aur id_token dono verify karta hai.
advantages: Zero dependency, poora code padh ke samjha ja sakta hai
ES256 keys aur signatures chhote hain (RSA se kaafi kam bytes)
disadvantages: Khud ka crypto glue code bugs ka risk; isliye interop tests zaroori
Sirf ek algorithm support
common_mistakes: DER signature seedha JWS mein daal dena
base64 (padding ke saath) use karna base64url ki jagah
Header ka alg verify karte waqt trust karna

question: How does verifyJwt protect against algorithm confusion, alg none, and tokens of the wrong type or audience?
answer_hinglish:
Algorithm confusion attack tab hota hai jab verifier token ke header ka alg trust karta hai. Attacker alg: none bhej deta hai (signature khali), ya alg: HS256 bhej ke public key ko HMAC secret ki tarah use karwa deta hai. Dono mein forged token valid lagta hai.

verifyJwt mein alg token se nahi liya jaata: agar header.alg !== 'ES256' toh turant JwtError. Phir typ check: /userinfo sirf typ at+jwt accept karta hai, isliye id_token (typ JWT) ko access token ki tarah use nahi kar sakte. kid se key milti hai; unknown kid reject. Signature exactly 64 bytes aur crypto.verify se. Uske baad iss exact, aud exact (string ya array mein), aur exp number hona chahiye aur now < exp.

Audience important hai: id_token ka aud client_id hai, access token ka aud issuer/userinfo. Agar aud check na ho, toh ek API ke liye bana token doosri API par chal jayega. Tests: userinfo.test.ts mein alg none, tampered signature, tampered payload, doosri key same kid ke saath, wrong audience, wrong issuer, expired, id_token presented -- sab 401.
why_needed: Signature check tabhi meaning rakhta hai jab verifier khud tay kare ki kaunsa algorithm aur kaunsi key; aur token sahi jagah ke liye bana ho.
real_world_analogy: Security guard ID card check karte waqt card par likha 'yeh card valid hai' nahi maanta; woh khud hologram check karta hai, aur dekhta hai ki card isi building ka hai, doosri building ka nahi.
how_it_works: Parse -> alg fixed ES256 -> typ match -> kid lookup -> signature verify -> iss -> aud -> exp. Har failure ek JwtError message ke saath, jise handleUserinfo 401 invalid_token mein badalta hai.
in_this_project: src/jwt.ts verifyJwt; src/server.ts handleUserinfo usse typ 'at+jwt' aur ctx.audience ke saath call karta hai, phir jti ki family revoked check karta hai. Mutations M11 (signature skip) aur M12 (audience skip) dono tests ne pakde. Note: M12 mein id_token wala test red nahi hua kyunki typ check bhi use rokta hai; dedicated wrong-audience test ne pakda.
advantages: alg none aur HS256 confusion design se hi impossible
typ se token types ka mix-up rukta hai
disadvantages: nbf aur clock skew handle nahi kiye (hamara apna server hai, isliye skew 0)
Sirf hamare issue kiye tokens verify karta hai, general purpose nahi
common_mistakes: Header ke alg se verify function choose karna
aud check bhool jana
id_token ko API access ke liye accept karna

question: What is the difference between the access token, the refresh token and the id_token issued here?
answer_hinglish:
Teen tokens, teen kaam.

Access token: API call karne ki permission. Yahan ES256 JWT hai, typ at+jwt, aud = issuer + '/userinfo', scope, client_id, jti, aur sirf 300 second chalta hai. Resource server (yahan /userinfo) ise Bearer header mein leta hai.

Refresh token: naya access token lene ke liye, bina user ko dobara login karaye. Yeh opaque hai (random 32 bytes, base64url) -- koi JWT nahi -- kyunki sirf authorization server ko ise samajhna hai. Server sirf iska SHA-256 hash store karta hai. 14 din chalta hai aur har use par rotate hota hai. Client ko tabhi milta hai jab uske grant_types mein refresh_token ho.

id_token: client ke liye proof ki user kaun hai aur kab login kiya. JWT hai, aud = client_id, nonce (jo client ne bheja tha), auth_time, at_hash. Sirf openid scope par milta hai, aur refresh par dobara nahi diya jaata.

Sabse common galti: id_token ko API par bhejna. Is server mein woh fail hoga kyunki /userinfo typ at+jwt aur apna audience maangta hai.
why_needed: Har token ka audience aur lifetime alag hai; ek hi token sab kaam kare toh leak ka nuksan sabse bada hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Access token = metro ka single journey token; refresh token = smart card jisse naye tokens nikal sakte ho (lekin sirf counter par); id_token = aapka ID card jo batata hai aap kaun ho, lekin uss se metro gate nahi khulta.
how_it_works: sendTokens ek family ke andar access token sign karta hai aur jti record karta hai; client.grant_types mein refresh_token ho toh random refresh token bana ke hash store karta hai; withIdToken ho toh id_token sign karta hai.
in_this_project: src/server.ts sendTokens. flow.test.ts pehla test teeno ke claims check karta hai; 'without the openid scope there is no id_token'; 'a client without the refresh_token grant gets no refresh token'; userinfo.test.ts 'the id_token presented as an access token ... -> 401'.

question: What is at_hash in the id_token, how is it computed here, and how was it tested?
answer_hinglish:
at_hash id_token ko us access token se bandhta hai jo usi response mein aaya. OIDC Core 3.1.3.6 ke hisaab se: id_token ke alg ka hash function lo (ES256 -> SHA-256), access token ke ASCII bytes ka hash nikalo, uska left-most half lo (256 bits ka aadha = 16 bytes), aur base64url karo. Result 22 characters ka hota hai.

Code flow mein at_hash optional hai (implicit/hybrid flow mein zaroori tha, jahan access token front channel se aata tha). Task ki shart thi ki implement karo toh sahi karo aur test karo, warna chhod do. Maine implement kiya, aur do tarah se test kiya: units.test.ts mein atHash ko ek independent createHash calculation se compare, aur flow.test.ts mein asli server ke id_token ka at_hash test ke andar khud calculate kiye hue value se match kiya -- yaani test hamare helper function par depend nahi karta.

Dhyan do: agar algorithm kabhi ES384 ho jaye toh hash SHA-384 aur 24 bytes hoga; abhi code sirf ES256 support karta hai, isliye atHash hardcoded SHA-256 hai.
why_needed: Client verify kar sakta hai ki access token badla nahi gaya (token substitution), kyunki id_token signed hai aur uska at_hash access token se match karna chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Parcel ke saath signed challan jisme parcel ka weight likha hai. Agar koi parcel badal de toh weight match nahi karega.
how_it_works: createHash('sha256').update(accessToken, 'ascii').digest().subarray(0, 16).toString('base64url').
in_this_project: src/jwt.ts atHash; src/server.ts sendTokens id_token claims mein at_hash: atHash(accessToken). Tests: flow.test.ts 'at_hash is the left half of SHA-256 over the access token (computed here independently)', units.test.ts 'at_hash = base64url(left 128 bits of SHA-256)'.
advantages: Token substitution detect ho sakta hai
Implement karna sasta
disadvantages: Code flow mein value kam hai kyunki dono tokens ek hi TLS response mein aate hain
Algorithm badle toh hash function bhi badalna yaad rakhna
common_mistakes: Poora hash daal dena, half nahi
Hex encoding use karna base64url ki jagah
Test mein usi helper se expected value banana (test kuch prove nahi karta)
follow_up_questions: c_hash kya hai aur yahan kyun nahi hai?

question: How are passwords and client secrets stored and verified, and how does the login avoid user enumeration by timing?
answer_hinglish:
Passwords aur confidential client secrets dono scrypt se hash hote hain (node:crypto ka scrypt, async version taaki event loop block na ho). Format hai scrypt$N$r$p$salt$hash -- parameters hash ke saath travel karte hain, toh kal cost badhani ho toh naye hashes naye params ke saath banenge aur purane bhi verify hote rahenge. Default N=2^17, r=8, p=1 jo OWASP ka minimum hai (lagbhag 128 MiB per hash); isliye maxmem explicitly set karna pada, warna node refuse karta hai.

Verify mein stored params aur salt se dobara scrypt, phir timingSafeEqual. parseSecretHash bounds check karta hai (N power of 2, 2^10 se 2^20) taaki galat config ek login par gigabytes memory na maange.

User enumeration: agar unknown username par turant 'invalid' bolo aur known par 100ms scrypt chalao, toh timing se attacker jaan lega kaunse usernames exist karte hain. checkPassword unknown user ke liye verifyAgainstDummy chalata hai -- same params ke saath scrypt -- aur message bhi same: 'Invalid username or password.' Timing maine measure nahi ki; sirf same code path aur same response test kiya hai.
why_needed: Database ya config leak ho toh plain ya fast hash (SHA-256) wale passwords GPU se jaldi crack ho jaate hain; scrypt memory-hard hai.
real_world_analogy: Lock jo kholne mein jaan-boojh ke 1 second leta hai: aapke liye koi farak nahi, lekin chor jo lakhon chaabiyan try karna chahta hai uske liye impossible.
how_it_works: hashSecret: random 16-byte salt, scrypt(secret, salt, 32, {N,r,p,maxmem}). verifySecret: parse -> scrypt -> timingSafeEqual. Tests ke liye N=2^14 wale hashes bante hain (fast), lekin code path same hai kyunki params hash se padhe jaate hain.
in_this_project: src/secrets.ts hashSecret, verifySecret, verifyAgainstDummy, parseSecretHash, DEFAULT_SCRYPT; src/server.ts checkPassword aur authenticateClient (unknown client par bhi dummy). src/hash-secret.ts CLI config ke liye hash banata hai. Tests: units.test.ts scrypt tests, login.test.ts 'unknown user -> same 401 and message as a wrong password'.
advantages: Memory-hard hash, offline cracking mehnga
Params hash mein, upgrade aasaan
Same response aur same kaam for unknown users
disadvantages: Har login par ~128 MiB aur kuch sau ms (measure nahi kiya), DoS ka target
libuv thread pool (default 4) logins ko queue kar sakta hai
common_mistakes: SHA-256 ya MD5 se password hash karna
Unknown user par jaldi return karna
=== se hash compare karna
follow_up_questions: argon2id vs scrypt vs bcrypt?
Client secret ke liye bhi scrypt zaroori hai ya SHA-256 kaafi hai?
Login DoS se kaise bachoge?

question: Why does the login form need a CSRF token, and how is it implemented in this server?
answer_hinglish:
Login CSRF ek kam famous lekin asli attack hai: attacker apni site se victim ke browser mein ek hidden form submit karwata hai jo authorization server par ATTACKER ke credentials se login karta hai. Ab victim attacker ke account mein logged in hai, aur jo data woh daalega (jaise card details) attacker ke account mein jayega. OAuth mein isse attacker apna code victim ke client session mein ghusa sakta hai.

Is server mein synchronizer token pattern hai. /authorize par ek LoginTransaction banta hai jisme random csrfToken hai; transaction ki id ek cookie (auth_tx, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/login) mein jaati hai aur csrfToken form ke hidden field mein. /login par cookie se transaction milta hai aur form ka csrf_token safeEqual se compare hota hai. Cross-site attacker victim ki cookie wala transaction ka token padh hi nahi sakta (same-origin policy), aur SameSite=Lax cross-site POST par cookie bhejta bhi nahi.

Tests: galat token, missing token, aur doosre transaction ka token -- teeno 403. Mutation M9 (check hata diya) ne teeno red kiye.
why_needed: Bina CSRF protection ke koi bhi site victim ke browser se hamara login form submit karwa sakti hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank counter par token number: aap tabhi transaction kar sakte ho jab aapke haath ka token counter ke record se match kare. Koi bahar se aapke naam par slip bheje toh token nahi hoga.
how_it_works: GET /authorize -> tx {id, csrfToken, params} save, Set-Cookie auth_tx=id, form mein csrf_token. POST /login -> cookie se tx -> expiry -> safeEqual(form.csrf_token, tx.csrfToken) -> credentials. Success par tx delete (single use) aur cookie Max-Age=0.
in_this_project: src/server.ts handleAuthorize (tx aur cookie), txCookie, handleLogin (CSRF check); src/pages.ts loginPage hidden field. Tests: test/login.test.ts 'bad CSRF token -> 403', 'a CSRF token from ANOTHER login transaction is rejected', 'missing transaction cookie -> 400'.
advantages: Token server side store, form ke hidden field se tamper nahi ho sakta
Authorize params bhi server side, form se dobara trust nahi
disadvantages: Ek browser mein ek hi login ek waqt par (cookie overwrite hoti hai)
Memory mein transactions, restart par khatam
common_mistakes: CSRF token cookie mein aur form mein same rakhna bina server-side binding ke, aur subdomain cookie injection bhool jana
Login form ko CSRF se exempt maan lena ('user to login hi nahi hai')
Token == se compare karna
follow_up_questions: SameSite=Lax akela kaafi kyun nahi?
Double-submit cookie pattern se yeh kaise alag hai?
Multi-tab login kaise support karoge?

question: Walk through safeEqual. Why hash both sides before timingSafeEqual, and where is it used?
answer_hinglish:
Normal === string compare pehle mismatch par ruk jaata hai. Agar attacker bahut baar try kare aur response time napey, toh theory mein woh ek ek character guess kar sakta hai (timing side channel). crypto.timingSafeEqual poore buffers ko hamesha same time mein compare karta hai -- lekin uski shart hai ki dono buffers ki length same ho, warna woh throw karta hai. Length ka check khud ek leak ho sakta hai.

safeEqual dono strings ka pehle SHA-256 nikalta hai -- dono 32 bytes ke ho jaate hain -- phir timingSafeEqual. Isse length difference bhi chhup jaata hai aur throw ka sawal nahi.

Kahan use hota hai: CSRF token compare (handleLogin) aur PKCE challenge compare (pkceMatches). Scrypt outputs ke liye seedha timingSafeEqual (verifySecret), kyunki woh hamesha 32 bytes hain. Authorization codes aur refresh tokens kabhi compare hi nahi hote: unka SHA-256 nikal ke Map key se lookup hota hai, toh secret khud kisi comparison mein nahi aata.

Honest note: maine timing measure nahi ki; units.test.ts sirf correctness test karta hai (same, different, alag length, empty).
why_needed: Secrets compare karte waqt timing leak se bachne ka standard tarika; aur timingSafeEqual ki length shart ko safely handle karna.
real_world_analogy: Exam checker jo har answer sheet ke saare sawal check karke hi result deta hai, chahe pehla sawal galat ho -- taaki time dekh ke koi andaza na laga sake ki kahan galti thi.
how_it_works: ha = sha256(a), hb = sha256(b), timingSafeEqual(ha, hb). SHA-256 collision practically impossible hai, isliye equality preserve hoti hai.
in_this_project: src/secrets.ts safeEqual; callers: src/server.ts handleLogin (CSRF) aur src/secrets.ts pkceMatches. Test: units.test.ts 'safeEqual compares contents, also for different lengths'.
advantages: Length leak aur throw dono se bachav
Ek function, har jagah same use
disadvantages: Do extra hashes (negligible cost)
Network jitter mein timing attack waise bhi mushkil; yeh defence-in-depth hai
common_mistakes: Length alag hone par jaldi return false karna
timingSafeEqual ko alag length buffers dena (exception)
Sirf passwords ke liye constant-time sochna, CSRF/PKCE bhool jana
follow_up_questions: Hash ke baad compare bhi constant-time kyun chahiye?
Lookup by hash kyun timing-safe maana?

question: How is the server structured so that the in-memory storage can later be replaced by a database?
answer_hinglish:
Saari state teen chhote interfaces ke peeche hai (src/store.ts): TransactionStore (login transactions), CodeStore (authorization codes) aur TokenStore (families, refresh tokens, access-token jti). Server sirf interfaces se baat karta hai; createAuthHandler options mein stores inject kiye ja sakte hain, default memoryStores().

Interfaces ko maine operations ke hisaab se design kiya, generic CRUD ke hisaab se nahi. Jaise CodeStore.consume(hash) ek hi method hai jo 'check used aur mark used' ek saath karta hai, aur TokenStore.markUsed(hash) boolean deta hai. Yeh isliye ki database implementation ko pata ho ki yahan atomicity chahiye: SQL mein UPDATE codes SET used = true WHERE hash = $1 AND used = false aur row count check. Agar interface get() aur set() hota, toh har implementation mein race condition ka chance hota.

Secrets sirf hash ke roop mein store hote hain (map keys sha256 hain), toh DB leak se codes ya refresh tokens nahi milte. Abhi limitations: ek process, restart par sab khatam, expiry sweep nahi. Yeh README mein 'Not implemented' mein likha hai, aur PLAN.md stage 2 mein PostgreSQL hai.
why_needed: Stage 1 ko simple rakhna tha, lekin aisa design nahi chahiye jo baad mein poora rewrite maange.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ki wiring mein switchboard: aaj bulb laga hai, kal LED lagao, wiring nahi badalni padti, kyunki socket standard hai.
how_it_works: AuthServerOptions.stores?: Stores. Ctx mein stores rakhe hain; handlers ctx.stores.codes.consume(), ctx.stores.tokens.markUsed() waghera call karte hain. Memory implementations Map use karti hain.
in_this_project: src/store.ts interfaces + MemoryTransactionStore, MemoryCodeStore, MemoryTokenStore, memoryStores(); src/server.ts AuthServerOptions.stores. test/helpers.ts startServer stores ko bahar rakhta hai taaki tests chahein toh dekh sakein.
advantages: Atomicity ki zaroorat interface mein hi dikhti hai
Tests bina DB ke fast chalte hain
DB add karna isolated change hoga
disadvantages: Interfaces abhi synchronous hain; DB ke liye Promise wale banane padenge aur handlers await karenge
Abhi ek hi implementation hai, toh abstraction asli DB par test nahi hui
common_mistakes: Generic get/set interface banana jisse atomic operations implementation par chhoot jaayein
Raw tokens store karna
Interface ke liye 'baad mein dekh lenge' bol ke global Maps directly use karna
follow_up_questions: Sync interface ko async banane mein kya badlega?
Redis vs PostgreSQL is state ke liye?
Contract tests dono stores par kaise chalaoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Operation-shaped interfaces (consume, markUsed) atomicity guarantee karte hain par har naya use case naya method maangta hai. Generic repository flexible hota par galti ki jagah deta.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar DB implementation consume ko SELECT phir UPDATE mein likhe, do concurrent redemptions dono jeet sakti hain aur do token families ban jayengi. Memory version mein yeh nahi hota kyunki Node single thread par check-and-set ek synchronous step hai.
advanced.alternatives: Redis with SET NX / Lua script for codes (TTL built-in), PostgreSQL for families aur refresh tokens; ya poora state Redis mein.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Multiple processes ke liye shared store zaroori; codes aur transactions ke liye TTL wala store (Redis) natural fit, refresh tokens ke liye durable DB. Signing key bhi sab processes mein same honi chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Async interfaces, PostgreSQL implementation, ek shared contract test suite jo dono stores par chale, expiry sweep job, aur concurrency test jo do redemptions ek saath bheje.

question: This project stores everything in memory. How would you design the database tables for codes, token families and refresh tokens?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle saaf bol dena: is project mein database nahi hai, sab src/store.ts ke Maps mein hai. Lekin design interfaces se seedha nikalta hai, toh main batata hoon kaise banata.

authorization_codes: code_hash (PK, SHA-256), client_id, redirect_uri, sub, scope (text[]), nonce, code_challenge, auth_time, expires_at, used boolean default false, family_id nullable. Consume = UPDATE ... SET used = true WHERE code_hash = $1 AND used = false RETURNING *; zero rows aaye toh alag SELECT se pata karo missing hai ya reused.

token_families: id (PK), client_id, sub, scope, auth_time, revoked boolean, created_at. Revoke = ek row update -- isiliye family model sasta hai.

refresh_tokens: token_hash (PK), family_id (FK, index), client_id, expires_at, used boolean. markUsed = UPDATE ... WHERE token_hash = $1 AND used = false, row count 1 matlab jeet.

access_token_jti: jti (PK), family_id, expires_at -- sirf jab tak access token zinda hai (300 s), toh cleanup job ise chhota rakhega.

login_transactions short-lived hain, unke liye Redis TTL better. Sab secrets hash hain, raw kabhi nahi.
why_needed: Restart aur multiple instances ke liye state durable aur shared honi chahiye, aur atomic operations DB level par.
real_world_analogy: Bank ka cheque register: har cheque number (hash) ek baar hi clear hota hai, aur cheque book (family) block karo toh uske saare cheque band.
how_it_works: Atomic conditional UPDATE race ko DB par chhodta hai; family_id index revoke check aur cascade ke liye; expires_at index cleanup ke liye.
in_this_project: Abhi sirf interfaces aur memory implementations: src/store.ts AuthorizationCode, TokenFamily, RefreshToken types inhi tables ke columns hain. Comments mein UPDATE ... WHERE used = false likha hai. PLAN.md stage 2 mein yeh kaam listed hai, NOT DONE.
advantages: Atomicity DB guarantee karta hai
Family revoke ek row update
Hash PK se lookup fast
disadvantages: Har refresh ek write
Used rows ki cleanup chahiye warna table badhti rahegi
common_mistakes: Raw token ko column mein rakhna
SELECT phir UPDATE (race)
Revoked family ke tokens ko alag alag delete karna instead of family flag
follow_up_questions: Reused code ko 'missing' se kaise alag karoge agar row delete kar di?
Cleanup job kitne der baad rows hataye?
Read replicas par revocation check karna safe hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Family flag sasta revoke deta hai lekin har refresh aur userinfo ko family join/lookup chahiye. Per-token revoked flag se lookup sasta par revoke mehnga.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Replica lag: revoke primary par hua, userinfo replica se padhe toh kuch second tak revoked token chal sakta hai. Cleanup job galti se unexpired used rows hata de toh reuse 'unknown' dikhega aur family revoke nahi hogi.
advanced.alternatives: Redis with TTL for codes aur jti (auto-expiry), PostgreSQL sirf families aur refresh tokens ke liye; ya event-sourced audit table.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: refresh_tokens sabse bada table banega; partition by expires_at ya regular purge. jti table ko Redis mein TTL ke saath rakhna better kyunki woh sirf 300 s ke liye hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Migrations, contract tests dono stores par, purge job with metrics, aur revocation checks hamesha primary se.

question: What happens if the same authorization code or refresh token is redeemed by two requests at the same moment? Why is it safe here, and what changes with several processes?
answer_hinglish:
Is project mein yeh safe hai kyunki Node ka JavaScript ek thread par chalta hai, aur MemoryCodeStore.consume mein 'used check' aur 'used = true' ek hi synchronous function mein hain, beech mein koi await nahi. Do HTTP requests kitni bhi jaldi aayein, unke handlers ek ke baad ek yeh step chalayenge: pehla ok paayega, doosra reused -- aur reused branch pehle wale ki family revoke kar dega. Refresh tokens mein bhi markUsed same pattern hai.

Ek subtle detail: refreshGrant mein rt.used ka check ek fast path hai, asli faisla markUsed karta hai. Kyunki DB ke saath do requests dono rt.used = false padh sakti hain; tab markUsed ka atomic UPDATE decide karega kaun jeeta. Isliye code mein dono hain aur comment likha hai.

Kai processes (cluster ya kai servers) mein memory store kaam hi nahi karega: code process A mein bana, token request process B par gayi toh 'invalid'. Shared store chahiye (Redis ya PostgreSQL) aur wahan atomicity conditional UPDATE ya Redis ke atomic command se. Signing key bhi sab processes mein same chahiye. Stage 1 explicitly single-process hai, maine concurrency test nahi likha.
why_needed: Single-use guarantees tabhi sach hain jab concurrent requests mein bhi sirf ek jeete; warna ek code se do token families ban sakti hain.
real_world_analogy: Ek hi coupon do counters par ek saath scan ho: agar dono counter alag register dekhte hain toh dono discount de denge. Ek central register jo 'scan + mark' ek saath kare, wahi bachata hai.
how_it_works: consume: e = map.get(hash); if (e.used) reused; e.used = true; ok -- sab synchronous. Async scrypt ya I/O is step ke beech nahi aata. DB mein equivalent: UPDATE ... WHERE used = false aur affected rows.
in_this_project: src/store.ts MemoryCodeStore.consume, MemoryTokenStore.markUsed; src/server.ts refreshGrant ka comment 'The atomic step...'. Tests sequential reuse cover karte hain (token.test.ts, refresh.test.ts); asli parallel concurrency test nahi hai -- yeh honest gap hai.
advantages: Bina locks ke correct (single process)
Pattern DB par seedha translate hota hai
disadvantages: Horizontal scaling bina shared store ke impossible
Agar koi future change beech mein await daal de toh race wapas aa sakti hai
common_mistakes: Sochna ki Node single thread hai toh koi race hi nahi -- await ke across race hoti hai
Check aur set ke beech DB call
Multiple instances mein in-memory store use karna
follow_up_questions: Ek parallel redemption test kaise likhoge?
Redis mein consume atomic kaise karoge?
Sticky sessions is problem ko solve karte hain?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Single process memory store simple aur correct hai par availability aur scale nahi deta. Shared store se scale milta hai par har request network hop aur DB ke failure modes laati hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Do processes bina shared store: random invalid_grant (code doosre process mein). Shared store with non-atomic consume: do families ek code se. Restart: saare codes aur refresh tokens khatam.
advanced.alternatives: Redis: SET used NX ya GETDEL for codes; PostgreSQL conditional UPDATE; ya single leader process jo token endpoint handle kare.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Token endpoint stateless ho jayega agar store shared ho; bottleneck DB writes (har refresh) aur scrypt (har login, CPU) banenge.
advanced.production_improvements: Shared store, concurrency test (Promise.all se do redemptions, exactly ek 200), shared signing key with rotation, aur health checks.

question: Access tokens here are self-contained JWTs. What does that cost for revocation, and how does this server handle it?
answer_hinglish:
JWT access token ka fayda: koi bhi resource server hamare /jwks se public key leke token offline verify kar sakta hai, har request par authorization server ko call kiye bina. Nuksan: jab tak exp nahi aata, token valid hai -- agar hum family revoke karein, ek third-party API jo sirf signature aur exp dekhti hai, use pata hi nahi chalega.

Is server ne yeh trade-off aise sambhala. Ek, access token ki lifetime chhoti hai: 300 second. Do, har access token ka jti us family se record hota hai (recordAccessToken). Hamara apna resource, /userinfo, signature ke baad jti ki family dekhta hai; family revoked ho toh 401. Isliye code reuse, refresh reuse aur /revoke ke baad /userinfo par access token turant marta hai -- tests yeh dikhate hain.

Lekin honest limitation: koi aur API jo hamare tokens offline verify kare, 300 s tak revoked token accept karegi. Alternatives: opaque access tokens + introspection (RFC 7662) -- har request par lookup, revocation turant, par latency aur AS par load. Ya JWT + chhota exp + introspection sirf sensitive operations ke liye. Stage 1 mein introspection nahi hai; PLAN.md mein hai.
why_needed: Har auth design ko yeh chunna padta hai: verification ki speed aur independence vs revocation ki immediacy.
real_world_analogy: Printed concert ticket vs digital ticket jo gate par live check hota hai. Printed ticket (JWT) gate bina internet ke check kar sakta hai, lekin cancel ho jaaye toh bhi gate ko pata nahi. Live check (introspection) turant cancel pakadta hai par har entry par server call.
how_it_works: sendTokens: jti = randomToken(16), recordAccessToken(jti, family.id). handleUserinfo: verifyJwt -> familyOfAccessToken(jti) -> getFamily -> revoked? 401.
in_this_project: src/server.ts sendTokens aur handleUserinfo; src/store.ts recordAccessToken, familyOfAccessToken. Tests: flow.test.ts revoke ke baad dono access tokens 401; token.test.ts reused code ke baad access token 401; refresh.test.ts reuse ke baad 401; revoke.test.ts 'an access token is not revocable here (only refresh tokens)'.
advantages: Resource servers bina AS call ke verify kar sakte hain
Hamara userinfo revocation turant honour karta hai
Chhoti lifetime se exposure bounded
disadvantages: Third-party offline verifiers ke liye revocation max 300 s late
jti record ek server-side state hai, toh 'fully stateless' nahi raha
common_mistakes: JWT ko revoke-able bolna bina batana ki kaun check karta hai
Access token ki lifetime ghanton ki rakhna
Revocation list ko har resource server par sync na karna
follow_up_questions: Introspection endpoint kaise design karoge, aur cache?
Sender-constrained tokens (DPoP) chori ka risk kaise kam karte hain?
300 s ki jagah 60 s kyun nahi?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Self-contained tokens availability aur latency jeetate hain (AS down ho tab bhi APIs chalti hain), opaque tokens control jeetate hain. Hybrid (chhota JWT + sensitive calls par introspection) aksar sweet spot hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Access token chori: 300 s tak kisi bhi offline API par chalega. AS restart bina SIGNING_KEY_FILE: nayi key, saare JWT turant invalid (yeh bhi ek tarah ka zabardasti revoke). jti store khali (restart) -> userinfo har purane token ko 401.
advanced.alternatives: Opaque + RFC 7662 introspection; JWT + revocation list push (pub/sub) to resource servers; DPoP-bound tokens; bahut chhote tokens (60 s).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: JWT verification CPU-bound hai aur har API node par scale hota hai; introspection AS ko hot path par daal deta hai aur cache chahiye, jo revocation ko phir se delay karta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Introspection endpoint, /revoke par access tokens ka deny-list, revocation events, DPoP, aur access token lifetime ko risk ke hisaab se tune karna (measure karke).

question: What breaks when this server restarts, and what would you change to survive restarts?
answer_hinglish:
Restart par do cheezein khatam hoti hain.

Pehli, saari state: login transactions, authorization codes, token families, refresh tokens aur jti records sab memory Maps mein hain. Restart ke baad user jo login form par tha usse 'Login expired' milega, jo code abhi jaari hua tha woh invalid_grant dega, aur har client ka refresh token invalid ho jayega -- matlab sabko dobara login.

Doosri, signing key: agar SIGNING_KEY_FILE nahi diya toh index.ts har start par generateSigningKey() karta hai. Nayi key ka naya kid hota hai, toh restart se pehle ke saare access tokens aur id_tokens kisi bhi verifier (hamara userinfo ya jose) mein 'unknown kid' / signature fail denge. Startup log mein keySource: generated likha aata hai taaki yeh dikh jaye.

Survive karne ke liye: SIGNING_KEY_FILE se stable key (yeh abhi bhi possible hai), persistent store same interfaces ke peeche (PostgreSQL), aur key rotation with overlap taaki key badalna bhi tokens na tode. Graceful shutdown abhi basic hai: server.close + idle connections close + 5 s force exit; iska test nahi hai.
why_needed: Deploy har restart hai; agar har deploy par sab users logout hon toh system production-ready nahi.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan ka register agar har shaam jal jaye: subah koi udhaar yaad nahi, sabko naya account kholna padega. Aur agar har din naya mohar (stamp) bane toh kal ki rasiden aaj fake lagengi.
how_it_works: createAuthHandler default stores memoryStores() aur default keys [generateSigningKey()]. index.ts SIGNING_KEY_FILE ho toh signingKeyFromPem.
in_this_project: src/index.ts (keySource log, SIGTERM handler), src/store.ts memoryStores, src/jwt.ts generateSigningKey / signingKeyFromPem. README 'Not implemented' aur 'Run it' section mein restart behaviour likha hai. Restart ka koi automated test nahi hai.
advantages: Stage 1 mein koi infra dependency nahi
Key file option se tokens restart ke baad bhi verify ho sakte hain
disadvantages: Restart = sab users logout
Key file disk par plain PEM, KMS/HSM nahi
common_mistakes: Production mein generated key ke saath chalana
Key badalte hi purani key JWKS se hata dena
Restart behaviour document na karna
follow_up_questions: Key rotation with overlap step by step kaise?
Private key kahan rakhoge (KMS, HSM)?
Rolling deploy mein do versions ek saath chalein toh?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Memory store aur generated key ne stage 1 ko zero-infra banaya; keemat har restart par poori state aur trust ka reset.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Crash loop: har restart nayi key, clients ke cached JWKS purane kid ke saath, sab tokens fail. Do instances alag generated keys ke saath: ek ka token doosre ke userinfo par fail.
advanced.alternatives: Key file (abhi), KMS-managed key jahan sign API call hai, ya JWKS mein multiple keys with rotation schedule.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Kai instances ko same key aur same store chahiye; key distribution aur rotation coordination ek alag concern ban jata hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Persistent store, KMS key, rotation with overlap (agli key pehle publish), shutdown test, aur startup check ki production mein keySource generated na ho.

question: A client reports invalid_grant from the token endpoint. How do you investigate which rule rejected it?
answer_hinglish:
invalid_grant ek chhatri error hai; asli wajah error_description mein hai, isliye pehle client se poora JSON body maango. codeGrant mein har check ka apna message hai:

'authorization code is invalid' -- code hamare store mein hai hi nahi: galat server (multiple processes ya restart, kyunki store memory mein hai), code copy karte waqt URL decoding galat, ya code kisi doosre issuer ka.
'authorization code was already used; tokens issued from it are revoked' -- client ne do baar bheja: double click, retry logic, ya browser ne callback page do baar load kiya. Yaad rakho iske baad pehle wale tokens bhi mar gaye.
'authorization code expired' -- 60 second se zyada laga: user ne callback page der se khola, ya client ka server slow.
'issued to another client' -- client_id mismatch, aksar do environments ke clients mix.
'redirect_uri does not match' -- token request ka redirect_uri authorize wale se byte-for-byte same nahi (trailing slash, http vs https).
'PKCE verification failed' -- verifier session mein kho gaya ya doosre tab ka verifier.

Refresh grant ke messages bhi alag hain, jaise 'refresh token reuse detected'. Agar code mein status sirf invalid_request hai, toh missing parameter hai (code_verifier ya redirect_uri).
why_needed: OAuth errors spec ne jaan-boojh ke generic rakhe hain; bina descriptive message ke production debugging andhere mein teer hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank cheque bounce karta hai toh 'returned' ke saath reason code deta hai: signature mismatch, date expired, insufficient funds. Reason ke bina aap andaza lagate rehte.
how_it_works: Har check oauthError(res, 400, 'invalid_grant', '<specific description>') ke saath return karta hai; responses no-store hain. Server abhi request logs nahi likhta, isliye description hi pehla clue hai.
in_this_project: src/server.ts codeGrant aur refreshGrant ke messages; tests har ek ko cover karte hain token.test.ts aur refresh.test.ts mein. Gap: server koi structured log nahi likhta (index.ts sirf startup line), toh server side se investigation abhi mushkil hai -- production mein log chahiye bina secrets ke.

# reproduce locally against the dev server
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9000/token \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code -d client_id=demo-spa \
  -d code=THE_CODE -d redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:5173/callback \
  -d code_verifier=THE_VERIFIER
# {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"authorization code expired"}

Error format standard, client libraries samajhti hain
disadvantages: Descriptions attacker ko bhi thoda batate hain (jaise code exist karta tha)
Server side logging nahi hai
common_mistakes: Sirf error code dekhna, description ignore karna
Retry logic jo token request dobara bhej ke reuse trigger kare
Redirect URI mein trailing slash ka farak ignore karna

question: Your team wants to put this server in front of real users next month. What would you insist on before that, based on what stage 1 does and does not do?
answer_hinglish:
Main seedha bolunga: stage 1 protocol ke security rules sahi aur tested hain, lekin yeh production-ready nahi hai, aur README ka 'Not implemented' list iska saboot hai.

Must-have before launch:
1. Persistent, shared storage (PostgreSQL/Redis) taaki restart aur multiple instances par users logout na hon, atomic consume/markUsed ke saath aur ek concurrency test.
2. Stable signing key KMS ya at least SIGNING_KEY_FILE se, aur rotation with overlap ka plan.
3. HTTPS ke peeche (issuer https; tab cookie mein Secure flag automatically lagta hai), aur http redirect URIs sirf loopback (config validator yeh already enforce karta hai).
4. Login rate limiting per username aur per IP -- abhi sirf ek transaction par 5 attempts hain, attacker naye transactions khol sakta hai. Saath mein scrypt cost ki wajah se login endpoint DoS target hai.
5. Structured logging aur metrics bina secrets ke (failed logins, reuse events, invalid_client).
6. Consent screen agar third-party clients hain, aur logout/session management.
7. Measurement: scrypt N=2^17 ki latency aur memory target machine par, token endpoint throughput. Abhi koi number nahi hai, aur main guess nahi dunga.
why_needed: Auth server sabse sensitive service hai; isme 'baad mein dekh lenge' ka matlab account takeover ho sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Naya bank vault design sahi hai aur lab mein test hua, lekin abhi alarm, CCTV, guard schedule aur backup generator nahi lage. Paise rakhne se pehle woh chahiye.
how_it_works: Har point ek existing gap se map hota hai: memoryStores, generateSigningKey default, maxLoginFailures per transaction, no logging, no consent.
in_this_project: README.md 'Not implemented (stage 1)' aur PLAN.md stages 2-5. src/server.ts maxLoginFailures (default 5), secureCookie (issuer https ho toh Secure), src/config.ts http sirf loopback.
advantages: Protocol rules tested aur interop-verified hain, foundation solid
Gaps documented hain, surprise nahi
disadvantages: Production ke liye kaafi kaam baaki
Khud ka auth server maintain karna lambi zimmedari hai
common_mistakes: Tests pass dekh ke production-ready bol dena
Rate limiting ko 'nice to have' samajhna
Bina measure kiye scrypt cost choose karna
follow_up_questions: Kya hum Keycloak ya managed service le lein? Kab khud ka banana sahi hai?
Login rate limiting ka design kya hoga?
Incident: refresh reuse alerts achanak badh gaye -- kya karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Khud ka AS control aur samajh deta hai, managed IdP operational bojh hata deta hai. Portfolio ke liye khud ka banana seekhne ke liye hai; real users ke liye main pehle managed option evaluate karunga.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Credential stuffing bina rate limit: account takeover aur scrypt se CPU/memory exhaustion. Restart par mass logout. Key leak bina rotation plan: saare tokens forge ho sakte hain.
advanced.alternatives: Keycloak, Ory Hydra, Auth0/Cognito; ya is server ko sirf internal tools ke liye limited scope mein.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Login CPU (scrypt) sabse pehle limit banega; libuv thread pool size aur alag login workers sochne padenge. Token endpoint DB writes par.
advanced.production_improvements: PLAN.md ke stage 2-5: persistent store, key rotation, rate limiting, consent, logout, DPoP, measurements, aur ek external security review.

question: What is the performance cost of using scrypt with N=2^17 for every login, and what has actually been measured?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honest jawab: is project mein koi performance measurement nahi hua. Stage 1 mein ek bhi number claim nahi kiya gaya, aur main andaza ko measurement bol ke nahi bechunga.

Jo design se pata hai: scrypt memory-hard hai. Memory lagbhag 128 * N * r bytes hai, yaani N=2^17, r=8 par 128 MiB per hash. Isliye code mein maxmem explicitly set hai, warna node default 32 MiB limit par refuse karta. Time typically sau milliseconds ke order mein hota hai (generic ballpark, machine par depend), lekin yahan measure nahi kiya.

Node mein async crypto.scrypt libuv ke thread pool par chalta hai (default 4 threads). Matlab event loop block nahi hota, lekin ek saath 4 se zyada logins queue mein wait karenge, aur 4 parallel logins 512 MiB memory le sakte hain. Isliye login endpoint ek DoS target hai -- rate limiting zaroori hai (abhi nahi hai).

Tests ke liye N=2^14 wale hashes bante hain taaki suite fast chale; production params ka path same hai kyunki params hash se padhe jaate hain. PLAN.md stage 5 mein scrypt latency aur memory measure karna listed hai.
why_needed: Password hashing ka cost hi security hai, lekin wahi cost capacity aur DoS ka risk bhi hai; dono ko measure karke balance karna padta hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank ke locker room mein ek waqt par sirf 4 log ja sakte hain aur har ek ko time lagta hai. Safe hai, lekin rush hour mein line lagegi -- aur koi jaan-boojh ke line bhar sakta hai.
how_it_works: scrypt(secret, salt, 32, {N, r, p, maxmem: 128*N*r + 16 MiB}) callback-based, libuv threadpool par. verifyAgainstDummy unknown users ke liye bhi same kaam karta hai, toh cost har attempt par lagti hai.
in_this_project: src/secrets.ts DEFAULT_SCRYPT, scrypt wrapper with maxmem; test/helpers.ts FAST params (N=2^14). README: 'No performance numbers are claimed'. PLAN.md stage 5.
advantages: Event loop block nahi hota (async)
Cost tunable, params hash mein
disadvantages: Memory per login bahut zyada
Thread pool contention, aur DNS/fs bhi usi pool ko share karte hain
common_mistakes: scryptSync use karke event loop block karna
maxmem set na karna aur 'invalid params' error par N ghata dena
Bina measure kiye cost choose karna ya numbers bata dena
follow_up_questions: UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE badhana kab sahi hai?
Aap ise kaise measure karoge (kya metrics)?
Login ko alag worker processes mein daalna?

question: How does client authentication work at the token and revocation endpoints, and why are only client_secret_basic and none supported?
answer_hinglish:
authenticateClient do raaste rakhta hai. Agar Authorization: Basic header hai, toh woh confidential client hona chahiye: base64 decode, pehle ':' par split, aur RFC 6749 2.3.1 ke hisaab se client_id aur secret ko form-urldecode (yeh detail aksar log bhoolte hain; openid-client isi encoding se bhejta hai aur interop test pass hota hai). Phir scrypt hash se verifySecret. Agar body mein bhi client_id hai aur Basic wale se alag hai toh invalid_request.

Header nahi hai toh body ka client_id ek PUBLIC client ka hona chahiye; confidential client bina Basic ke 401. Public client ka Basic header bhi refuse hota hai, kyunki uske paas secret hota hi nahi. client_secret body mein aaye (client_secret_post) toh seedha invalid_client -- ek hi method support karke attack surface chhota rakha.

Unknown client ya public client ke Basic par bhi dummy scrypt chalta hai taaki timing se client ids pata na chalein. Failure par 401 invalid_client aur WWW-Authenticate: Basic (RFC 6749 5.2). Ek detail: failed client auth code ko burn nahi karta, kyunki request grant tak pahunchi hi nahi -- test 'wrong client secret' yeh dikhata hai.
why_needed: Confidential client ka code chura ho toh bhi bina secret ke tokens nahi milne chahiye; aur public client ko galti se confidential treat nahi karna.
real_world_analogy: Office building: employees (confidential) badge swipe karte hain; visitors (public) sirf naam register karte hain aur unhe sirf lobby tak jaane diya jaata hai. Visitor ka fake badge swipe bhi reject.
how_it_works: parseForm -> authenticateClient(req, params) -> {ok, client} ya {status, error}. handleToken aur handleRevoke dono isi function ko use karte hain.
in_this_project: src/server.ts authenticateClient, BASIC_CHALLENGE; src/config.ts confidential ke liye client_secret_hash zaroori, public ke liye mana. Tests: token.test.ts '/token client authentication' block (6 tests), revoke.test.ts 'client authentication is required', interop.test.ts confidential client ClientSecretBasic ke saath. Mutation M10 pakda gaya.
advantages: Ek hi secret method, kam confusion
Secrets hashed, config leak se secret nahi milta
Public/confidential ka strict separation
disadvantages: Shared secrets phir bhi bearer jaise hain; private_key_jwt ya mTLS behtar
scrypt per token request CPU cost
common_mistakes: Basic credentials ko urldecode na karna (special chars wale secrets fail)
Public client ko secret ke bina confidential ki tarah allow karna
invalid_client par 400 dena aur WWW-Authenticate na bhejna
follow_up_questions: private_key_jwt kaise kaam karta hai?
Client secret ke liye scrypt overkill hai kya, high-entropy secret ke liye SHA-256?
mTLS client auth ka setup?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Ek method support karna simple aur auditable hai, par kuch clients ko adapt karna padega. scrypt secret hashing consistent hai par high-entropy server-generated secrets ke liye SHA-256 bhi defensible hota aur sasta.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Secret leak (client ke server se): attacker tokens le sakta hai jab tak secret rotate na ho; rotation ka mechanism abhi nahi hai (config edit + restart). scrypt cost se token endpoint par CPU DoS.
advanced.alternatives: private_key_jwt (RFC 7523), tls_client_auth (RFC 8705), ya client_secret_post (jo yahan jaan-boojh ke nahi hai).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Har confidential token request ek scrypt; 100x par yeh dominate karega. Options: SHA-256 for high-entropy secrets, ya verified-secret cache (risk ke saath).
advanced.production_improvements: Secret rotation with two active secrets, private_key_jwt, per-client rate limits, aur invalid_client events ka monitoring.

question: Write a vitest integration test proving that a reused authorization code fails and also kills the access token issued from it.
answer_hinglish:
Test ka idea: real server ephemeral port par chalao, poora front channel (authorize -> login form with CSRF -> redirect) karke ek code lo, use redeem karo, check karo ki access token /userinfo par chalta hai, phir wahi code dobara bhejo. Doosri request invalid_grant aur no-store deni chahiye, aur ab pehla access token /userinfo par 401 aur refresh token invalid_grant dena chahiye.

Dhyan dene wali baat: sirf 'second redemption fails' check karna kaafi nahi. Woh toh tab bhi pass hoga agar server reuse par revoke karna bhool jaye. Isliye assertion pehle wale tokens par bhi hai. Maine yeh mutation M4 mein verify kiya: revokeFamily ko disable kiya toh yahi test red hua, aur koi doosra nahi.

Helpers test/helpers.ts mein hain: startServer (issuer = asli port, injectable clock), getCode (front channel), redeem (token request), userinfo. Repo mein yeh test token.test.ts mein 'a reused code fails AND revokes the tokens issued from it' naam se hai; neeche wahi trimmed hai.
why_needed: Security rule ka test tabhi kaam ka hai jab rule ka poora asar check kare, sirf error code nahi.
real_world_analogy: Fire alarm test mein sirf ghanti bajna check nahi karte, yeh bhi check karte hain ki sprinkler chala aur darwaze khule.
how_it_works: getCode -> redeem (200) -> userinfo (200) -> redeem again (400 invalid_grant) -> userinfo (401) -> refresh (invalid_grant).
in_this_project: test/token.test.ts 'a reused code fails AND revokes the tokens issued from it'; helpers test/helpers.ts; implementation src/server.ts codeGrant reused branch.
advantages: Real HTTP, real cookies, real redirects
Rule ka side effect bhi verify
disadvantages: Integration test unit test se dheema
Third-party offline verifier par revocation test nahi karta (kyunki wahan hota hi nahi)
common_mistakes: Sirf second request ka status check karna
Fixed port use karna (parallel runs mein clash)
Mutation se verify na karna ki test fail ho sakta hai
follow_up_questions: Isi tarah refresh reuse ka test kaise likhoge?
Parallel redemption ka test kaise likhoge?

question: What are the discovery document and the JWKS endpoint for, and how is the kid chosen?
answer_hinglish:
Discovery document (/.well-known/openid-configuration) ek JSON hai jo client libraries ko batata hai ki server kahan aur kya karta hai: issuer, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, userinfo_endpoint, jwks_uri, revocation_endpoint, aur supported cheezein -- response_types ['code'], code_challenge_methods ['S256'], id_token signing ['ES256'], token_endpoint_auth_methods ['client_secret_basic', 'none']. openid-client ka discovery() isi ko padhta hai; isliye maine dhyan rakha ki document sirf wahi bole jo sach mein implement hai.

JWKS (/jwks) public signing keys ko JWK format mein publish karta hai: kty EC, crv P-256, x, y, alg ES256, use sig, aur kid. Private part (d) kabhi nahi. Resource server token ke header ka kid dekh ke JWKS se sahi key chunta hai.

kid kaise: RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint -- crv, kty, x, y members ko lexicographic order mein bina whitespace ke JSON banao aur SHA-256 base64url. Fayda: kid key se deterministic hai, alag se store nahi karna padta. Discovery aur JWKS dono Cache-Control public, max-age=300 bhejte hain. Test discovery.test.ts thumbprint ko dobara calculate karke match karta hai.
why_needed: Bina discovery ke har client mein URLs hardcode; bina JWKS ke resource servers ko key manually deni padti aur rotation impossible hota.
real_world_analogy: Discovery = mall ka directory board (kaunsi dukaan kahan); JWKS = bank ka public signature specimen card jisse koi bhi cheque ka signature match kar sake.
how_it_works: discoveryDocument(issuer) static JSON banata hai. signingKeyFromPrivate publicKey.export({format: 'jwk'}) karta hai aur jwkThumbprint se kid.
in_this_project: src/server.ts discoveryDocument aur route mein /jwks; src/jwt.ts jwkThumbprint, signingKeyFromPrivate. Tests: discovery.test.ts; interop.test.ts mein jose createRemoteJWKSet aur openid-client discovery dono isi par chalte hain.
advantages: Clients auto-configure hote hain
Deterministic kid
Key rotation ka raasta (JWKS mein kai keys)
disadvantages: Galat discovery document clients ko galat raaste par bhejta hai
JWKS cache (300 s) key change ko delay karta hai
common_mistakes: Discovery mein unsupported features advertise karna
JWKS mein private key leak
kid ko random rakhna aur restart par badalna bina purani key publish kiye
follow_up_questions: Key rotation mein JWKS cache ka kya problem hai?
issuer mismatch par client kya karta hai?

question: How did you prove that the security tests can actually fail, and what did that process find?
answer_hinglish:
Green tests ka matlab tabhi kuch hai jab rule tootne par woh red hon. Maine 15 security rules ke liye manual mutation check kiya: source mein rule jaan-boojh ke toda, poora suite chalaya, dekha kaunse tests red hue, phir git checkout se source wapas, aur aakhir mein poora suite green. Har result README ki table mein hai.

Udaharan: redirectUriAllowed mein includes ki jagah startsWith -> 3 redirect tests red. plain PKCE allow -> 2 tests red. PKCE verify skip -> 3 red. Reuse par revoke hataya -> sirf 'a reused code fails AND revokes...' red. CSRF check hataya -> 3 red. Signature check hataya -> 4 red. state hataya -> 6 red, jinme 4 openid-client interop tests (kyunki library state check karti hai).

Sabse kaam ki baat ek gap mila: markUsed ko 'mark' karna band kiya (rotation khatam) toh sirf reuse wala test red hua. Rotation test ka naam tha 'the old one stops working' lekin woh sirf check kar raha tha ki teen tokens alag hain -- purana token dobara try hi nahi karta tha. Fix: test ab purana token bhejta hai aur invalid_grant expect karta hai; mutation dobara chala ke dono tests red dekhe. Aur ek observation: audience check hatane par id_token wala test red nahi hua kyunki typ check bhi use rokta hai -- isliye dedicated wrong-audience test zaroori tha.
why_needed: Security code mein ek test jo kabhi fail nahi ho sakta, false confidence deta hai -- jo bina test ke code se bhi bura hai.
real_world_analogy: Smoke detector ki battery check karne ke liye uske paas jaan-boojh ke dhuan karte ho. Sirf green light dekh ke maan lena ki kaam karta hai, galti hai.
how_it_works: Edit (break) -> npx vitest run -> FAIL lines note -> git checkout -- src -> repeat. Baseline commit pehle kiya taaki restore exact ho.
in_this_project: README.md 'Proving the tests can fail (mutation checks)' table M1-M15 aur 'Gap found'. Fix test/refresh.test.ts 'every use returns a NEW refresh token; the old one stops working'. Koi mutation tool (Stryker) use nahi kiya; yeh manual tha.
advantages: Har security test ki effectiveness ka saboot
Kamzor test (galat naam, adhoora assertion) pakda gaya
disadvantages: Manual hai, har change par dobara nahi chalta
Sirf chune hue 15 mutations; baaki code par nahi
common_mistakes: Test ke naam par bharosa karna, assertions na padhna
Mutation ke baad source restore bhool jana
Helper se expected value banana jisse test tautology ban jaye
follow_up_questions: Stryker jaisa tool CI mein kaise lagaoge?
Mutation score kitna kaafi hai?
Kaunsa rule abhi bhi bina mutation check ke hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Manual mutations sasta aur focused hai (sirf security rules), automated mutation testing poora coverage deta hai par dheema aur noisy hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Future refactor koi assertion hata de aur suite green rahe; manual check dobara nahi chala toh gap chupchap wapas aa sakta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Stryker Mutator for TypeScript, property-based tests, ya security rules ke liye dedicated negative test checklist jo PR template mein ho.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Codebase badhe toh manual mutations unmanageable; tool se sirf src/server.ts aur src/jwt.ts jaisi critical files par mutation run chalana practical hai.
advanced.production_improvements: CI mein Stryker critical files par, mutation table ko script se generate karna, aur har naye security rule ke saath ek mutation entry.

question: An attacker steals the authorization code from the redirect URL. Walk through what each protection in this server does.
answer_hinglish:
Chalo step by step dekhte hain ki chura hua code attacker ke kaam aata hai ya nahi.

1. PKCE: token endpoint par code_verifier chahiye. Verifier sirf legit client ke paas hai (session mein), URL mein kabhi nahi gaya. Attacker galat ya missing verifier bhejega -> invalid_grant ya invalid_request. Yeh sabse badi deewar hai.
2. Code burn: attacker ka galat-verifier wala attempt bhi code ko burn kar deta hai. Ab legit client redeem kare toh 'already used' milega aur user ko dobara login karna padega -- ek DoS, lekin token leak nahi.
3. Agar legit client pehle redeem kar chuka hai aur attacker baad mein code bheje: reuse detect hota hai aur us code ki family revoke -- legit client ke tokens bhi. Yeh jaan-boojh ka trade-off hai (RFC ki recommendation): chori ke signal par sab band.
4. Client binding: code sirf usi client_id ke liye; confidential client ke liye attacker ko secret bhi chahiye (Basic).
5. Expiry: 60 second ke baad code bekaar.
6. redirect_uri exact match: attacker apna redirect_uri daal ke code apne paas mangwa hi nahi sakta.

Jo yahan nahi hai: agar attacker client ke andar hi baitha ho (XSS in SPA) toh woh verifier bhi padh sakta hai -- PKCE wahan nahi bachata.
why_needed: Redirect URL leak hona realistic hai (logs, Referer, extensions); system ko maan ke chalna chahiye ki code leak hoga.
real_world_analogy: Chor ne aapka locker ki parchi chura li, lekin locker kholne ke liye aapka fingerprint (verifier) bhi chahiye; aur parchi ek baar use hote hi bekaar, aur agar dobara dikhe toh bank aapka locker bhi seal kar deta hai.
how_it_works: codeGrant ka order: required params -> consume (burn) -> reused? revoke -> expiry -> client -> redirect_uri -> pkceMatches -> issue.
in_this_project: src/server.ts codeGrant; tests token.test.ts: 'wrong code_verifier', 'the code is burned by its first presentation, even a failed one', 'a reused code fails AND revokes...', 'a code issued to another client', 'an expired code'; authorize.test.ts redirect_uri tests.
advantages: Kai layers: ek tootey toh doosri bachaye
Chori ka attempt detectable
disadvantages: Attacker code burn karke legit login ko fail kara sakta hai
Client ke andar XSS ke khilaf PKCE kaam nahi karta
common_mistakes: Sochna ki HTTPS ke baad code leak ho hi nahi sakta
PKCE ko optional rakhna
Code ko lamba (minutes) valid rakhna
follow_up_questions: Galat verifier par code burn na karte toh kya trade-off hota?
iss parameter (RFC 9207) mix-up attack se kaise bachata hai?
SPA mein XSS ke baad kya bachta hai?
